verdict: Avoid new aluminium exposure in Korba: the data call is AVOID (27) and local signals are worse than India; lend only to asset-backed downstream fabricators with verified offtake, and decline smelter-linked and power-intensive proposals.
title: Korba aluminium & aluminium products: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Korba's aluminium story is a smelter town, not a fabrication cluster.** The anchor asset is the Korba (P) smelter, which ran Søderberg cells and then prebake cells using Chinese technology [2]; Wood Mackenzie's note is dated April 2026 and is a paid asset report, so treat it as background, not current operating data. **Cash in this business is made by converting alumina and power into metal and selling at the London price** — so the borrower's margin is the gap between the metal price and its power-plus-alumina cost, not a value-added spread. **Downstream units — extrusion, conductors, rolled products — buy metal at the smelter gate and sell to state utilities and construction**, and their cash sits in receivables from those buyers. **Collect from customer** the split between own-metal and bought-metal, power tariff, and receivable days before you size anything.

## What has changed now
**The local economy is running behind India.** Chhattisgarh GST collections grew +2.4% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, and electricity demand +6.7% against +9.5% [D] — both local stress signals. **Brent at $113/bbl sits above the $75–100 band [D]**, which matters because smelting is power-intensive and coal logistics are fuel-linked. **Labour disruption at BALCO stopped work in April 2026 [3]** — a local report, and the only Korba-specific operating news we have; it is seven months old. **India-wide aluminium output (NIC 24) grew only +2.4% YoY [D]**, so the national volume picture is modest even as prices are strong.

## Where the growth is — and who to avoid
**Peer results are strong but they are the producer's story, not the fabricator's.** Vedanta Aluminium's Q2FY27 revenue rose 41% to INR 22,066 crore with EBITDA of INR 10,192 crore at ~46% margin [4], and production hit a record 649,000 tonnes, up 5% [6]. **Management expects net effective price in H2 to be about $50 lower than Q2 [5]** — so do not underwrite fabricators on today's metal price. **Pursue downstream fabricators with firm utility or PSU offtake, own premises, and metal bought on back-to-back orders.** **Avoid smelter-dependent ancillaries, power-intensive remelters, and any proposal whose repayment assumes the current price holds**; a rating note on a similar borrower flags margins staying sensitive to international aluminium prices and global logistics [10].

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the metal, not the balance sheet.** Take hypothecation of stock and receivables with a charge on the smelter-gate purchase contract, and keep tenor inside the order cycle. **Ask for the monthly metal purchase invoice and the buyer's acceptance every month**, plus GST returns and bank statements. **If the proposal's receivable days exceed the customer's stated credit terms, ask for the ageing and the top-three buyer names.** Where promoters support the unit through unsecured interest-free loans — seen at Rs 135 crore in one rated peer [10] — treat that as a cushion, not as repayment capacity.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the local demand pulse first.** If Chhattisgarh GST growth slips further below India's +6.1% [D], tighten new sanctions. **If the borrower's power bill per tonne rises while realisations fall, ask for the revised cost sheet and reprice.** **If a labour action at the anchor smelter recurs [3], expect downstream dispatches to stall — ask for the dispatch register.** **If Brent stays above $113/bbl [D], stress-test the borrower at a lower metal price, given the expected $50 H2 price decline [5].**
watch: Chhattisgarh GST growth falls further below India's +6.1% [D] -> freeze new sanctions, review existing limits
Power cost per tonne rises while realisation falls -> ask for revised cost sheet, reprice or reduce limit
Metal purchase invoices and buyer acceptances (monthly)
Receivable days exceed stated credit terms -> ask for ageing and top-three buyer names
Brent stays above $113/bbl [D] or metal price falls toward the expected $50 H2 decline [5] -> stress-test and cut tenor
Labour action at the anchor smelter recurs [3] -> ask for dispatch register, hold disbursement
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Local GST and power demand trail India; Brent above band; Korba labour stoppage reported.
